newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on USDA export sales data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on USDA export sales data.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed sharply higher on a larger-than-expected number for corn in USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
"The numbers again tell us we're not curtailing usage at these price levels," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended April 3 totaled 929,500 tonnes, well above expectations for 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
USDA's data included sales to Taiwan of 203,600 tonnes. There had been ideas that Taiwanese corn purchases would be trimmed due to foot and mouth disease in its hogs.
A cutback in Taiwan's hog herd was seen trimming that country's feed requirements.
Corn futures also found support from the wet and cold weather in the northern U.S. Midwest which was leading to concerns about delays in seeding the crop.
But most traders agreed that the strong corn number in USDA's sales report led the rally.
"It was all exports in corn and beans," said Ron Kucha, also of O'Connor.
Corn closed 1/2 to 5-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 4-3/4 at $3.03-3/4 a bushel.
Corn rallied to the day's highs in late dealings with demand broad-based, but mostly speculative.

"A lot of that (gain) was the export sales report but the market didn't look all that spiffy until late," said John Kleist, director of agricultural research for ING Futures and Options. Even at a million metric tonnes, it's (exports) been so erratic, $3.00 corn is hard to maintain."

Traders said funds bought roughly 15.0 million bushels of corn led by Prudential Securities purchase of three million December and two million May, traders said. Refco Inc bought two million bushels of July, Cargill Inc bought five million December and two million May and ADM Investor Services bought two million May, traders said.
ABN Amro-Chicago Corp sold at least 15.0 million bushels of July, traders said.

In spread trading, USA Trading did three million bushels of May/July at one cent, premium July, traders said. Dean Witter did one million July/May at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 cents, SAK Futures spread one million July/May at 1-1/2 cents, premium July and Farmers Commodities Corp did one million July/May at 1-3/4 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn volume was estimated by the CBOT at 62,000 contracts. The estimate was below Wednesday's volume of 78,144 contracts.
In corn options, USA Trading sold 1,000 July $2.80 calls at 28 cents, bought 1,000 July $3.00 calls at 15-3/4 cents and bought 200 July $2.10 calls at 94-1/2 cents, traders said.
Iowa Grain sold 1,500 May $2.90 puts at one to 1-1/4 cents, they said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, above the 15,707 traded Wednesday.
